title: Étale deformation chart and its smooth projection
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $d\geq0$, put $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, and let $C\to R$ be an étale ring map (so the induced affine-scheme morphism is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]). Write $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)R$, $E=C[t,x_1/t,\ldots,x_d/t]\subseteq C[t,t^{-1}]$, and $D=R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$. The canonical map $R\otimes_C E\to D$ is an isomorphism. Under $E\cong A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ with $x_i\mapsto t u_i$, using affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ is étale, and its composite with the affine-space projection [def-sbc-affine-space] $\operatorname{Spec}A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]\to\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Clause (2), local deformation algebra $C[t,J/t]$, flat tensor injection, and étale base change

proof.text: Put $P=A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$. Evaluation $t\mapsto t$, $u_i\mapsto x_i/t$ gives a map $\phi:P\to C[t,t^{-1}]$. Its image is $E$: the image contains the stated generators of $E$, because $x_i=t(x_i/t)$, and conversely all images lie in $E$. For injectivity write a polynomial as a finite sum $\sum_{a,\beta}c_{a,\beta}t^a u^\beta$, where $a\geq0$, $\beta\in\mathbb N^d$ and $|\beta|=\sum_i\beta_i$. Its image is $\sum_{a,\beta}c_{a,\beta}x^\beta t^{a-|\beta|}$. The exponent pairs $(\beta,a-|\beta|)$ are distinct for distinct $(a,\beta)$; uniqueness of the coefficients of polynomial/Laurent monomials over $A$ therefore implies that the kernel is zero. Thus $\phi:P\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ is an $A[t]$-algebra isomorphism, with the $C$-algebra structure on $P$ given by $x_i\mapsto tu_i$. This uses no domain or reducedness assumption.

By hypothesis the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is étale. It is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] implies that $C\to R$ is a flat ring map. Equivalently $R$ is a flat $C$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow C[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective as a map of $C$-modules. Apply the left-tensor exactness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to $0\to E\xrightarrow{j}C[t,t^{-1}]\to C[t,t^{-1}]/E$. It follows that $1\otimes j:R\otimes_C E\to R\otimes_C C[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective. The quotient here is a module quotient; $E$ need not be an ideal.

source.place: Tags 00HB (definition-flat), 00HD (lemma-flat); affine translation is Morphisms Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize)

proof.text: The tensor algebra universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives the ring map $\alpha:R\otimes_C C[t,t^{-1}]\to R[t,t^{-1}]$, $r\otimes\sum_n c_nt^n\mapsto\sum_n r\bar c_nt^n$. Its inverse is $\sum_n r_nt^n\mapsto\sum_n r_n\otimes t^n$. This is additive and multiplicative by the coefficient formula for Laurent multiplication; balancing over $C$ gives $r\bar c\otimes t^n=r\otimes ct^n$, so the composites are identities on Laurent monomials and pure tensors, hence on all finite sums. Thus $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. The composite $\alpha(1\otimes j)$ has image exactly $D$: every pure tensor maps to a product of an element of $R$ and an expression in $C$, $t$, and $x_i/t$, hence lands in $D$; conversely it contains $R$, $t$, and each $\bar x_i/t$. For $f\in I$ write $f=\sum_i r_i\bar x_i$; then $f/t=\sum_i r_i(\bar x_i/t)$ is in the image. These elements generate $D$ by its definition. Step 2 gives injectivity of the composite, proving that its corestriction is precisely the canonical isomorphism $R\otimes_C E\xrightarrow{\sim}D$.

source.place: Clause (2), the explicit flat tensor identification of the deformation chart; tensor universal property as in Stacks Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $C$ and its two algebras $R$ and $E$. Together with Step 3 this identifies $\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}E$, with the map to $\operatorname{Spec}E$ induced by $e\mapsto1\otimes e$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] applies to the assumed étale map $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ and the arbitrary map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, giving an étale projection. Under the isomorphism $P\cong E$ of Step 1 its ring map is $P\to D$, $t\mapsto t$, $u_i\mapsto\bar x_i/t$. By the contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], this is exactly the induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ in the statement.

source.place: Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); étale stability is Morphisms Tag 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale)

proof.text: By the affine description of [def-sbc-affine-space], the projection $p:\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ is the affine $d$-space projection over $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$. Therefore [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] says that $p$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. The map $a:\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ of Step 4 is étale in the sense of [def-weil-etale-morphism]; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] it is smooth of relative dimension $0$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] with this $a$, $m=0$, and $f=p$, $n=d$. The composite $p\circ a$ is smooth of relative dimension $0+d=d$, as required. No nonemptiness or surjectivity of $a$ is required.
